restoration_note: The teaching is a sevenfold contemplation of the sun as the fashioned likeness (ⲡⲉⲓⲛⲉ) of the First Greatness, with seven goods of light met by seven wickednesses of night. Most gaps are small completions of words bisected by line breaks (ⲡⲟⲩⲁⲓⲛⲉ at {0} and {8}, ⲛⲃⲉⲗ at {10}, ⲃⲓ at {4}) or restored ordinal/circumstantial markers (ⲧⲧ- prefixes at {2}, {3}; circumstantial ⲉ- at {5}). The editorial proposals fit Coptic grammar and the surviving parallel sequences within the chapter (ⲧⲧⲙⲁⲍⲥⲛⲉⲩ, ⲧⲧⲙⲁⲍϣⲁⲙⲧ, ⲕⲁⲧⲟⲟⲧⲟⲩ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ, ϣⲁϩⲃⲓ). Gap {1} (~6 chars at the end of line 8 before a large lacuna spanning lines 9–26) is too weakly constrained — it begins a constituent whose continuation is lost — and is left unrestored.

restorations.basis: Completes ⲡⲟⲩⲁⲓⲛⲉ 'the Light' bisected by line break; the standard Manichaean phrase ⲡⲓⲛⲁⲟ̄ ⲛ̄ⲁⲓⲱⲛ ⲛⲧⲉ ⲡⲟⲩⲁⲓⲛⲉ 'great Aeon of the Light' = the Land of Light, the Father's celestial state to which the sun-icon points (cf. lexicon: Land of Light, Light = Divine Truth in its illuminating quality).

~6 character lacuna at the end of line 8, followed by a large lost block (lines 9–26) before the visible text resumes. The phrase 'great Aeon of the Light' is grammatically complete, so {1} begins a new constituent whose continuation is lost. No formula or trace constrains the fill enough to choose among 'the Living,' 'the Holy,' a new clause, or another phrase; better left unrestored than smoothed.

Feminine definite-article + ordinal stem ⲧⲧϣⲁⲣⲡ̄, matching the explicit parallel sequence ⲧⲧⲙⲁⲍⲥⲛⲉⲩ ('the second' line 31), Ⲧⲙⲁϩϥ̄ⲧⲁⲩ ('the fourth' line 43), Ⲧⲙⲁϩ†ⲟⲩ (fifth, 46), Ⲧⲙⲁϩⲥⲁⲩ (sixth, 49), Ⲧⲙⲁϩⲥⲁϣϥ (seventh, 52). Editor's reading retained.

ⲧⲧⲙⲁⲍⲥⲛⲉⲩ 'the second,' the second item in the sevenfold series of goods (rest and peace = quieting of the will once the understanding is illumined). Article + status form; standard Lycopolitan ordinal series.

Completes ϣⲁϩⲃⲓ 'he bears (away),' the same verb used in line 33 ϣⲁϩⲃⲓ ⲍⲱⲱϩ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ ⲙ̄ⲙⲁⲩ 'he himself takes away from them.' Visible ⲃ + lost ⲓ; English 'bea{4}' completes as 'bears.' Spiritual sense: the Light bears away the falsity-darkness from the midst of the natural mind.
Circumstantial converter ⲉ- producing ⲉⲩⲣⲁⲓⲥ 'while watching' (the wakeful ones keeping fearful vigil before their encampments). One-letter trace at line start; English 'w' completes 'watching.'

Echoes line 39 ⲕⲁⲧⲟⲟⲧⲟⲩ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'they cease their hand'; here in circumstantial: ⲉⲩⲕⲁⲧⲟⲟⲧⲟⲩ ⲛ̄ⲣⲁⲓⲥ 'while ceasing their watch of vigil.' Expanded slightly beyond the editor's ⲕⲁⲧⲟ to give the full circumstantial form with the doubled ⲟⲟ attested in line 39, fitting the line-start position.

Standard formulaic close ⲁⲭⲱⲩ ⲍⲙ ⲡⲕⲟⲥⲙⲟⲥ 'upon them in the cosmos,' completing the third good (the light shining forth upon men in the cosmos). Parallels ⲁⲭⲱⲩ at line 28 (light shines upon them) and the recurrent ⲍⲙ̄ ⲡⲕⲟⲥⲙⲟⲥ formula. Visible -ⲟⲥⲙⲟⲥ is what survives.

Final ⲉ of ⲡⲟⲩⲁⲓⲛⲉ; preceding ⲡⲟⲩⲁⲓⲛ visible. The seventh good explicitly names the sun as ⲡⲙⲉⲓⲛⲉ ⲙ̄ⲡⲡⲣⲓⲉ ⲛ̄ⲧⲉ ⲛⲁⲓⲱⲛ ⲙⲡⲟⲩⲁⲓⲛⲉ 'the sign of the Radiance of the aeons of the Light' — the consummating revelation that the visible icon points back to the Father's celestial state.

The standard ϣⲁ ⲟⲩⲏⲡ ⲧⲉ idiom 'for some (portion) it is …' introducing the next discriminating clause. Editor's restoration retained as an established Coptic formula and good fit for the surviving traces.

Final ⲗ of ⲛ̄ⲃⲉⲗ 'eyes' (lexicon: ⲡⲃⲉⲗ = eye = the understanding). Confirmed by line 71 ⲛ̄ⲛⲣⲱⲙⲉ ⲙⲟⲩϩ ⲛ̄ⲕⲙⲏⲙⲉ 'of men are filled with darkness' — the precise inversion of the first good (light entering the eyes), where night now refills the eyes/understanding with falsity.
